attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I'm really excited about this paper. My overall impression is excellent, and I'd be very happy to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b08/review-experiment-om1k7apq/call-181985545ed846228610394989e93b18/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, os
for name in ['pypdf', 'pdfplumber', 'fitz', 'pypdfium2', 'PIL']:
 print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
print('files', os.listdir('.'))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
 text=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(text)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'--- PAGE {i+1} ---\\n'+p.read_text() for i,p in enumerate(sorted(Path('tmp/pdfs').glob('page-*.txt')))))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-14.txt tmp/pdfs/page-15.txt tmp/pdfs/page-16.txt tmp/pdfs/page-17.txt tmp/pdfs/page-18.txt tmp/pdfs/page-19.txt'

strengths: Significance: PMVB offers a practical way to incorporate predictions into commercial MIP solvers by adding cardinality constraints. Compatibility with logistic regression, GNNs, and LP relaxation solutions makes the approach potentially useful across applications.

Soundness of the algorithmic core: Solving all four complementary subproblems preserves global optimality independently of prediction quality. Table 2 reports useful exact-solving speedups of 1.11–1.31, including a reduction from 1283 to 979 seconds on MKP-L.
Originality: Using prediction-accuracy statistics to choose cardinality tolerances offers an interpretable perspective on integrating learned solutions with established branching methods.

Presentation, limitations, and ethics: The workflow and distinction between heuristic and exact solving are generally clear. The manuscript provides a code link, hardware information, and dataset-generation details, and openly acknowledges the strong independence assumption and possible infeasibility of LP-derived neighborhoods. No material research-ethics concern is apparent.
weaknesses: Soundness—central probability guarantee: Theorem 2.1 does not follow from Lemma 2.1. The lemma bounds classification error averaged over instances, whereas equation (4) uses this as a correctness bound for a fixed instance and prediction-selected group. High marginal accuracy does not imply high accuracy conditional on predicting one. Moreover, independence at fixed ξ in A4 does not establish the independence needed under the joint training/test distribution. Consequently, the Hoeffding argument does not establish the advertised containment guarantee.

Soundness—practical calibration: Theorem 3.1 is valid given its population mean and variance conditions, but the manuscript does not establish these conditions from finite validation data after selecting τ. Remark 3.1 further replaces threshold-based counts with summed prediction scores; these stronger constraints do not inherit the theorem without additional calibration assumptions. Empirical coverage measurements are absent. The experimental δ = 0.8 also provides only a 20% lower bound for each constraint individually, offering little support for the high-confidence interpretation.

Soundness—data-free analysis: Theorem 4.1 bounds the number of LP-selected variables omitted by the integer optimum, then asserts that the opposite-direction bound follows by complementation. These two disagreement counts need not agree because the solutions can select different numbers of items. A separate argument is required to establish the second inequality.

Evaluation—selection bias: Section 5.4 reduces 132 MIPLIB instances to 57 by excluding immediately infeasible restricted subproblems and joint timeouts. Infeasible restrictions are relevant method failures, so the reported 16% improvement describes a selected subset rather than performance across the benchmark. Evaluation should include all instances with failure rates and the cost of a specified fallback.

Evaluation—scope of speedup evidence: Section 5.2 measures time to a target chosen by PMVB's own 120-second run. This is informative but insufficient to establish generally superior primal performance without fixed-budget objective gaps, externally specified targets, or primal-integral results. Timeout handling and prediction overhead are unclear. Results lack uncertainty estimates, and SCUC has only five test instances per configuration.

Originality and attribution: Cardinality/local branching and prediction-guided neighborhoods are established approaches, as the manuscript acknowledges through references [13,14,23,31]. Comparisons primarily against unmodified solvers do not isolate the contribution of probabilistic threshold selection. Comparisons using the same predictor with existing neighborhood methods, together with threshold and calibration ablations, are needed to establish the incremental advance.

Reproducibility and presentation: Important experimental details remain unspecified, particularly the variance estimates used to construct constraints, solver versions, and several test-set specifications. The data-free confidence parameters are not adequately connected to an implementable calibration procedure. Table 4 contains only 30 entries, including a duplicated blp-ar98, despite reporting 57 evaluated instances. These omissions impede independent verification of the main empirical claims.
